opening.text: Think about the last time you packed for a long trip. You did not wait until the car was running. You made a list. You checked the weather. You put in the things you would need. And when the day came, you walked out the door calm and ready.
The Savior has told us He will come again. We do not know the day. But we can pack. We can get ready, a little at a time, so that the day brings joy and not worry.
I would like to talk about the Second Coming of Jesus Christ.

mainMessage.text: Jesus Christ will return to the earth. The scriptures say so plainly. No one knows when. But the Lord has told us how to be ready. We listen to His prophets. We stand in holy places. We keep our lamps filled. And we use today to prepare, because this life is the time to prepare to meet God. For those who are ready, His coming will be a day of hope.

blocks.text: He will come again.

When the Savior rose into heaven, two angels spoke to His disciples. They said He would return in the same way He left. And the Lord has told us what that day will bring. He will come with power and glory, and He will live on the earth in righteousness.

And when he had spoken these things, while they beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight. And while they looked steadfastly toward heaven as he went up, behold, two men stood by them in white apparel; Which also said, Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye gazing up into heaven? this same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven.
For I will reveal myself from heaven with power and great glory, with all the hosts thereof, and dwell in righteousness with men on earth a thousand years, and the wicked shall not stand.
Elder Bruce R. McConkie of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles wrote this in his book Mormon Doctrine, page 640. It is a book, not a conference talk.

Those being resurrected with celestial bodies, whose destiny is to inherit a celestial kingdom, will come forth in the morning of the first resurrection. Their graves shall be opened and they shall be caught up to meet the Lord at his Second Coming. They are Christ’s, the firstfruits, and they shall descend with him to reign as kings and priests during the millennial era.
His coming is good news for those who love Him.
No one knows the day.

People have guessed dates for centuries. The Savior said it is not for us to know. Even the angels do not know. Only the Father knows. So the Lord gave us something better than a date. He gave us a way to live.
But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only.
Watch therefore, for ye know neither the day nor the hour wherein the Son of man cometh.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles asked these questions in his talk “Preparation for the Second Coming” from the April 2004 general conference.

What if the day of His coming were tomorrow? If we knew that we would meet the Lord tomorrow—through our premature death or through His unexpected coming—what would we do today? What confessions would we make? What practices would we discontinue? What accounts would we settle? What forgivenesses would we extend? What testimonies would we bear? If we would do those things then, why not now? Why not seek peace while peace can be obtained?
If we would do it then, why not now? That is the heart of it.
We can be ready, like the wise virgins.

The Savior told a story about ten young women waiting for a bridegroom. Five were wise and had oil for their lamps. Five were not. The Lord has said that when He comes, this parable will be fulfilled. The wise are those who have taken the Holy Spirit as their guide.

And at that day, when I shall come in my glory, shall the parable be fulfilled which I spake concerning the ten virgins. For they that are wise and have received the truth, and have taken the Holy Spirit for their guide, and have not been deceived—verily I say unto you, they shall not be hewn down and cast into the fire, but shall abide the day.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks said this in the same talk, “Preparation for the Second Coming,” from the April 2004 general conference.

The arithmetic of this parable is chilling. The ten virgins obviously represent members of Christ’s Church, for all were invited to the wedding feast and all knew what was required to be admitted when the bridegroom came. But only half were ready when he came.
The point is not to scare us. It is to wake us up. The oil is our daily faithfulness, and it is built one day at a time.
The Lord warns us through His prophets.

A good packing list comes from someone who has checked the weather. The Lord does the same for us. He does nothing without telling His servants the prophets. And He gave His disciples a simple lesson. When the fig tree puts out leaves, summer is near. In the same way, we can learn to recognize the signs.
Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.

Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is nigh: So likewise ye, when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors.
President Ezra Taft Benson said this in a teaching recorded in The Teachings of Ezra Taft Benson, page 133. It is a book, not a conference talk.

When the prophet points out the sins of the world, the worldly, rather than repent of their sins, either want to close the mouth of the prophet or else act as if the prophet didn’t exist. Popularity is never a test of truth. Many a prophet has been killed or cast out. As we come closer to the Lord’s second coming, you can expect that as the people of the world become more wicked, the prophet will be less popular with them.
Listening to the prophet is not always popular. But it is how we stay ready.
We stand in holy places.

The Lord gave us a simple instruction for the last days. Stand in holy places, and do not be moved. A holy place can be a temple. It can also be a home, a chapel, or a quiet room where we pray. It is anywhere we choose to do what is right.
But my disciples shall stand in holy places, and shall not be moved; but among the wicked, men shall lift up their voices and curse God and die.
Wherefore, stand ye in holy places, and be not moved, until the day of the Lord come; for behold, it cometh quickly, saith the Lord. Amen.
President Thomas S. Monson said this in his talk “Dare to Stand Alone” from the October 2011 general conference.

As we go about living from day to day, it is almost inevitable that our faith will be challenged. We may at times find ourselves surrounded by others and yet standing in the minority or even standing alone concerning what is acceptable and what is not. Do we have the moral courage to stand firm for our beliefs, even if by so doing we must stand alone? . . . May we ever be courageous and prepared to stand for what we believe, and if we must stand alone in the process, may we do so courageously, strengthened by the knowledge that in reality we are never alone when we stand with our Father in Heaven.
We may stand alone sometimes. But we are not alone.
Today is the time to prepare.
Alma taught that this life is the time to prepare to meet God. Not later. Not when things calm down. Now. He urged us not to put off repentance. Time in this life is a gift, and we can use it well.

For behold, this life is the time for men to prepare to meet God; yea, behold the day of this life is the day for men to perform their labors. And now, as I said unto you before, as ye have had so many witnesses, therefore, I beseech of you that ye do not procrastinate the day of your repentance until the end; for after this day of life, which is given us to prepare for eternity, behold, if we do not improve our time while in this life, then cometh the night of darkness wherein there can be no labor performed.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Now Is the Time to Prepare” from the April 2005 general conference.

Brothers and sisters, we live to die and we die to live—in another realm. If we are well prepared, death brings no terror. From an eternal perspective, death is premature only for those who are not prepared to meet God. Now is the time to prepare. Then, when death comes, we can move toward the celestial glory that Heavenly Father has prepared for His faithful children.
That is a hopeful way to look at it. Preparing is how we find peace.

story.title: Noah builds the ark

blocks.text: Noah was told by the Lord that a flood was coming. There was no rain yet. But God told him what to do.

And God said unto Noah, The end of all flesh is come before me; for the earth is filled with violence through them; and, behold, I will destroy them with the earth. Make thee an ark of gopher wood; rooms shalt thou make in the ark, and shalt pitch it within and without with pitch. . . . Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he.

Noah did not wait for the sky to darken. He built when there was no sign of rain. He did exactly what the Lord asked. That is what preparing looks like. We act on the Lord’s word before we see the storm.

application.text: First, pretend the Savior will come tomorrow. Write down what you would do today. Then do one of those things this week. Second, check your own lamp. Are you praying, reading the scriptures, and going to the sacrament? Pick one habit to strengthen. Third, think of one “holy place” in your life, and make it a little more holy.

story.title: Simeon waits in the temple

blocks.text: Simeon was an old man in Jerusalem. He had waited a long time for the Savior. The Holy Ghost had told him he would see the Lord’s Christ before he died.

And, behold, there was a man in Jerusalem, whose name was Simeon; and the same man was just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel: and the Holy Ghost was upon him. And it was revealed unto him by the Holy Ghost, that he should not see death, before he had seen the Lord’s Christ. And he came by the Spirit into the temple: and when the parents brought in the child Jesus, to do for him after the custom of the law, Then took he him up in his arms, and blessed God, and said, Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word: For mine eyes have seen thy salvation, Which thou hast prepared before the face of all people; A light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel.

Simeon waited in the temple, and he was guided by the Spirit. When the day came, he knew the child. He was ready, and he was at peace. We wait for the Savior’s second coming in a similar way. We stay near the Spirit, and we stay close to holy places.

application.text: First, this week, spend a few quiet minutes in a holy place. Go to the temple grounds, a chapel, or a quiet room at home. Second, write down one thing you would want to settle before the Lord comes, such as an apology or a forgiveness, and take one step toward it. Third, read the words of the latest general conference talk and follow one piece of counsel.

story.title: The faithful and wise servant

blocks.text: The Savior taught a short parable about a servant whose master was away. The master could return at any time.

Who then is a faithful and wise servant, whom his lord hath made ruler over his household, to give them meat in due season? Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing. Verily I say unto you, That he shall make him ruler over all his goods.

The servant did not stand at the window all day. He did his work. He cared for the household. When the master came, he was found doing what he should. That is the picture of readiness. We are not asked to stare at the sky. We are asked to be faithful in our daily work.

application.text: First, choose one “guest ready” habit for your home this week, such as a family prayer, a scripture, or a hymn. Second, do one thing you have been putting off, such as an apology, a visit, or a call. Third, ask yourself each night, “If the Savior came tomorrow, would I be at peace?” Then adjust.

What confessions would we make? What practices would we discontinue? What accounts would we settle? What forgivenesses would we extend? What testimonies would we bear? If we would do those things then, why not now? Why not seek peace while peace can be obtained?
Practice now, and the real day will not catch us off guard.
We prepare in ordinary ways.

The Lord told of ten young women who went out to meet a bridegroom. Five had extra oil. Five did not. He said that on the day of His coming, this parable will be fulfilled. The wise are those who have the truth and have the Holy Spirit as their guide. That kind of readiness is built a little at a time.

And at that day, when I shall come in my glory, shall the parable be fulfilled which I spake concerning the ten virgins. For they that are wise and have received the truth, and have taken the Holy Spirit for their guide, and have not been deceived—verily I say unto you, they shall not be hewn down and cast into the fire, but shall abide the day.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks taught this in the same talk, “Preparation for the Second Coming,” from the April 2004 general conference.

The arithmetic of this parable is chilling. The ten virgins obviously represent members of Christ’s Church, for all were invited to the wedding feast and all knew what was required to be admitted when the bridegroom came. But only half were ready when he came.
Praying, reading, and serving may seem small. They are the oil.
We follow the instructions of those who know.

In a drill, we listen to the one in charge. The Lord has given us prophets for this reason. He will do nothing without revealing it to them. And He taught us to learn from the fig tree. When the leaves come, summer is near.
Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.

Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is nigh: So likewise ye, when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors.
President Ezra Taft Benson taught this in a message recorded in The Teachings of Ezra Taft Benson, page 133. It is a book, not a conference talk.

When the prophet points out the sins of the world, the worldly, rather than repent of their sins, either want to close the mouth of the prophet or else act as if the prophet didn’t exist. Popularity is never a test of truth. Many a prophet has been killed or cast out. As we come closer to the Lord’s second coming, you can expect that as the people of the world become more wicked, the prophet will be less popular with them.
Popularity is not the test. Truth is.
We know where safe places are.
In a drill, you know where the exit is. The Lord has told us where to stand. Stand in holy places. Do not be moved. Those places are where the Spirit is, and where we feel peace.
But my disciples shall stand in holy places, and shall not be moved; but among the wicked, men shall lift up their voices and curse God and die.
Wherefore, stand ye in holy places, and be not moved, until the day of the Lord come; for behold, it cometh quickly, saith the Lord. Amen.
President Thomas S. Monson taught this in his talk “Dare to Stand Alone” from the October 2011 general conference.

As we go about living from day to day, it is almost inevitable that our faith will be challenged. We may at times find ourselves surrounded by others and yet standing in the minority or even standing alone concerning what is acceptable and what is not. Do we have the moral courage to stand firm for our beliefs, even if by so doing we must stand alone? . . . May we ever be courageous and prepared to stand for what we believe, and if we must stand alone in the process, may we do so courageously, strengthened by the knowledge that in reality we are never alone when we stand with our Father in Heaven.
We stand together with our Father in Heaven.
We use the time we have.

Alma taught that this life is the time to prepare to meet God. A drill only helps if we take it seriously. The same is true here. We should not delay repentance, because the time to do the work is now.

For behold, this life is the time for men to prepare to meet God; yea, behold the day of this life is the day for men to perform their labors. And now, as I said unto you before, as ye have had so many witnesses, therefore, I beseech of you that ye do not procrastinate the day of your repentance until the end; for after this day of life, which is given us to prepare for eternity, behold, if we do not improve our time while in this life, then cometh the night of darkness wherein there can be no labor performed.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles taught this in his talk “Now Is the Time to Prepare” from the April 2005 general conference.

Brothers and sisters, we live to die and we die to live—in another realm. If we are well prepared, death brings no terror. From an eternal perspective, death is premature only for those who are not prepared to meet God. Now is the time to prepare. Then, when death comes, we can move toward the celestial glory that Heavenly Father has prepared for His faithful children.
No terror. That is the promise of being prepared.

story.title: Joseph stores grain in Egypt

blocks.text: Joseph in Egypt had been told that seven good years would come, followed by seven years of famine. So during the good years, he got to work.

And in the seven plenteous years the earth brought forth by handfuls. And he gathered up all the food of the seven years, which were in the land of Egypt, and laid up the food in the cities: the food of the field, which was round about every city, laid he up in the same. And Joseph gathered corn as the sand of the sea, very much, until he left numbering; for it was without number. . . . And the seven years of plenteousness, that was in the land of Egypt, were ended. And the seven years of dearth began to come, according as Joseph said: and the dearth was in all lands; but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.

Joseph did not wait for the famine. He prepared while times were good. When the hard years came, there was bread. That is what the Lord asks of us. We build our faith in the good years, so that we have it when we need it.

application.text: First, think of a “drill” you can practice each day. It might be a morning prayer or a few verses of scripture. Do it for one week. Second, find out one way you can follow the prophet’s latest counsel more fully. Third, store some spiritual “grain” this week. Write down one testimony moment so you can read it in a hard season.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that Jesus Christ will come again. I know that He has told us how to be ready. I know that the prophets guide us in these days. I know that preparing brings peace and not fear. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: Most homes have a flashlight in a drawer. We hardly think about it. But the night the power goes out, we want to know two things. Where is it? And do the batteries work? Nobody checks the batteries in the dark.
The Savior told a story about oil in lamps. It is the same idea. The time to check is before the lights go out. I would like to talk about the Second Coming, and how we can be ready for it.

mainMessage.text: Jesus Christ will come again. No one knows the day. The Lord has not left us to guess. He has told us to listen to the prophets, to keep the Holy Spirit as our guide, to stand in holy places, and to use this life to prepare. If we do, we can wait with peace. That day can be one of the best days we have ever known.

blocks.text: He has promised to return.

When Jesus went up into heaven, two angels stood by the disciples. They said He would come back in the same way. In our day, the Lord added that He will come with great power and glory, and that He will live on the earth with the righteous.

And when he had spoken these things, while they beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight. And while they looked steadfastly toward heaven as he went up, behold, two men stood by them in white apparel; Which also said, Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye gazing up into heaven? this same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven.
For I will reveal myself from heaven with power and great glory, with all the hosts thereof, and dwell in righteousness with men on earth a thousand years, and the wicked shall not stand.
Elder Bruce R. McConkie of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles wrote this in his book Mormon Doctrine, page 640. It is a book, not a conference talk.

Those being resurrected with celestial bodies, whose destiny is to inherit a celestial kingdom, will come forth in the morning of the first resurrection. Their graves shall be opened and they shall be caught up to meet the Lord at his Second Coming. They are Christ’s, the firstfruits, and they shall descend with him to reign as kings and priests during the millennial era.
It is a promise, and it is a happy one.
We will not see it on a calendar.
People have tried to name a date. The Savior said that no one knows the day or the hour, not even the angels. He wanted us to watch, not to calculate. So we keep a steady habit of readiness.
But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only.
Watch therefore, for ye know neither the day nor the hour wherein the Son of man cometh.

Those five young women were invited. They knew what to do. Readiness is a choice made in small ways.
The Lord tells us ahead of time.

A good neighbor gives a warning when a storm is on the way. The Lord does the same through His prophets. He does nothing without revealing it to them. And He gave His disciples a simple picture. When the fig tree puts out leaves, summer is near. We learn to read the signs.

The warning is a kindness. We can be grateful for it.
We stay where the light is.

The Lord said to stand in holy places and not be moved. Holy places are where the Spirit lives. They can be a temple, a chapel, or a home where people pray together. There is light in them, and that is where we want to be.

We may stand alone for a moment. We are never alone.
The time is now.
Alma said this life is the time to prepare to meet God. He asked us not to put off repentance. Time in this life is a gift, and it will not last forever. The best day to start is today.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time about preparing for the Second Coming. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The ten virgins

blocks.text: The Savior told this parable Himself. Ten young women took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.

Then shall the kingdom of heaven be likened unto ten virgins, which took their lamps, and went forth to meet the bridegroom. And five of them were wise, and five were foolish. They that were foolish took their lamps, and took no oil with them: But the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps. While the bridegroom tarried, they all slumbered and slept. And at midnight there was a cry made, Behold, the bridegroom cometh; go ye out to meet him. Then all those virgins arose, and trimmed their lamps. And the foolish said unto the wise, Give us of your oil; for our lamps are gone out. But the wise answered, saying, Not so; lest there be not enough for us and you: but go ye rather to them that sell, and buy for yourselves. And while they went to buy, the bridegroom came; and they that were ready went in with him to the marriage: and the door was shut. Afterward came also the other virgins, saying, Lord, Lord, open to us. But he answered and said, Verily I say unto you, I know you not. Watch therefore, for ye know neither the day nor the hour wherein the Son of man cometh.

Notice that all ten fell asleep. Being ready did not mean never resting. It meant having oil when the cry came. The five who were ready had done their part before the night. We cannot give another person our faith in an hour. But we can build it every day, and we can help others build theirs.

application.text: First, ask yourself what your “oil” is. Prayer, scripture study, the sacrament, service. Pick the one that needs the most care this week. Second, help someone else fill their lamp. Invite them to church, read with them, or serve beside them. Third, trust the Lord’s timing, and do not try to guess dates.
